# First-use record

This directory is an SDK-only public-interface author trial. It uses the SDK README, sdk.json, public CLI index/help, docs/spatial-batches.md, generated canonical types, and a newly generated OS-temp project. No repository source, prior audits, implementation tests, rubric, network, install, commits or external account actions were used. The parent supplied only the task, allowed paths and external analyzer location. Later parent messages asked for progress and reminded that replays must not mutate sealed evidence.

The exact recorded exploration/execution argv is in the numbered operation JSON files, with raw .stdout/.stderr, exit code, timeout and elapsed time. Operation 000 bootstraps the recorder before exploration. Its record describes the bootstrap rather than reproducing its full shell body; its console result is retained separately. Every SDK exploration/execution after bootstrap is recorded before process start. This bootstrap recording limitation is explicit.

First strict success: 026. First successful submission: 027 (one update, no delivered geometry). First delivered geometry: 028 (two updates). The first authored project is retained including its JSON BOM error; the final project changes only that JSON encoding. There were no Luau type errors and no source fallback. sourceFallbackStep is null. First-use authoring ended at operation 028; subsequent steps build and exercise the independent replay verifier.

Natural author/tool guesses are separate from intentional negative inputs in FIRST-USE.json. All failures are retained. The query example uses canonical SpatialBody, SpatialQuery, SpatialHit, SpatialBatchResult and EngineApi; project-authored code contains no any, cast or stub. The unchanged bundled canonical block itself contains upstream legacy any annotations for unrelated APIs.

The public guide led directly to spatial.create/submit/take and complete observation publication; no invented spatial API calls were attempted. The natural search "scene entity" returned no matches. This did not prove a missing capability; canonical EntityApi plus a narrower entity.getPosition search supplied the read-only sentinel observation. The first official check --types failed on a UTF-8 BOM produced by Windows PowerShell; the original bytes remain in first-authored-project. Rewriting JSON without BOM allowed the first actual analyzer invocation to pass.

The independent probe initially found no Python executable, then encountered the Windows process execution policy and a PowerShell vector-expression bug. The raw exits and original verifier are retained. The repaired PowerShell-only verifier passed without changing example Luau.

## Geometry authored independently

Category bits are synthetic. IDs 17, 41 and 4294967295 are at center distance 3 with radius 0.5 and category 1. A nearer ID 0 at x=0.25 is category 2, and moving ID 73 is category 4. The masked nearest query excludes ID 17 and therefore chooses ID 41 over the equal-distance larger ID. The category-1 overlap radius is 2.5, so all three radius-0.5 spheres touch; output order must be 17, 41, 4294967295.

The query center moves from x=0 to x=10 while body 73 moves from x=12 to x=8. Relative center separation is 12-14t, and combined radius is 1. First contact is t=11/14, query travel distance 55/7, body center 62/7, body-facing surface point 117/14, and normal (-1,0,0). The zero-ID query independently selects category 2 and checks the unsigned numeric record path.

The replay verifier computes all records with generic double-precision Euclidean nearest/overlap and a standard quadratic moving-sphere equation, then compares IDs/order and every distance/fraction/point/normal field with an author-selected absolute tolerance of 0.00002. That threshold is this probe's threshold; it is not asserted to be an SDK-provided universal GPU tolerance.

Tick 1 rejects a duplicate-ID replacement, submits version 1, rejects same-tick take, mutates caller body/query tables, installs a valid 48-byte USB1 packed replacement as version 2, submits again, and destroys the live index. Tick 2 receives both frozen versions with the original geometry and the all-empty replacement, then rejects ticket reuse. The unrelated scene entity retains all observed fields and coordinates (-23,47). The independent verifier also checks complete capability limits and live usage.

## Contract interpretation versus execution

Executed: official SDK CLI native headless run, official external luau-analyze via check --types, direct complete info/batch/query-result observation publication, frozen inputs, numeric ID max-u32 and zero, version preservation after invalid replacement, packed repair, next-tick delivery, one-shot consumption, and unchanged scene entity. The backend reports cpu, external=false. No GPU initialization or execution was performed, no rendered player claim is made, and CLI timing is not a performance claim.

Interpreted only from docs/spatial-batches.md: CPU is the default and allocates no GPU device. Exported players read spatial_backend in player.presentation.json; cpu uses the Rust reference, gpu requires working compute/bridge, and auto attempts GPU initialization then falls back to CPU if unavailable. Native players may override the host policy with --spatial-backend. Execution failure after initialization remains an error. Embedders select an executor before the first tick; host-owned resources are possible. CPU/GPU scan the same bounded records; GPU v1 reads results back and is not GPU-resident simulation/rendering.

The contract dispatches frozen work only after successful script/physics phases. Earliest delivery is next tick even on CPU; official Web hosts wait for GPU completion before advancing it, while native local dispatch currently waits. Invalid execution/device completion faults do not fabricate empty results. Cancel/reload retires old tickets; successful reload preserves indices/versions/backend, failed reload preserves the live manager and allocator. These device/reload boundaries were not exercised by this example. The session schema was inspected and no reload command was invented.

Observation finding retained: direct publication of empty Luau hits tables yields {} rather than [] in native JSON. Non-empty arrays, full hit records, max-u32 ID and safe_integer=9007199254740991 are preserved. The probe reports this empty-shape deviation explicitly rather than rewriting raw evidence.

## Replay

Final example files: final-project/AGENTS.md, final-project/player.presentation.json, final-project/project.unone.json, final-project/scenes/main.scene.json, final-project/scripts/main.luau. The standalone case is case.json. Verify-Probe.ps1 is the replayable generic probe and verification; Verify-Probe-first.ps1 preserves the first broken verifier.

Run from any directory in Windows PowerShell:
`powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<this-directory>\Verify-Probe.ps1"`

Optional -Sdk, -Analyzer and -OutputDirectory override defaults. OutputDirectory must be new and under OS temp. The verifier reads final-project and case.json, copies the example into a fresh OS-temp project, then writes command-before-execution records and raw CLI output only into that temp output. It never writes to this evidence directory during replay. The process policy flag applies to this invocation only. A successful run writes verification.json and independent-expected.json beside the raw reports. replay-run retains this trial's successful verifier output.

SHA256SUMS.json hashes every evidence artifact's bytes and length except itself and SEAL.txt; SEAL.txt contains the detached manifest hash. No mutation follows sealing.
